channel.title: Pakistan Provincial Reform Institute (PPRI) — Policy Research Feed
channel.description: Peer-reviewed policy papers, empirical reports, datasets, and constitutional legal analysis on provincial reform, federalism, and municipal devolution in Pakistan.

item.title: New Administrative Units in Pakistan 2026: What Is Actually Being Proposed?
item.description: Pakistan’s 2026 administrative-units debate explained: proposals for 12–15 new provinces, 160 empowered local governments, Article 239 supermajorities, and verified legal status.

item.title: Provinces of Pakistan 2026: Names, Capitals, Population and Area
item.description: A factual guide to Pakistan’s four provinces, capitals, 2023 census populations and area—plus the difference between provinces, territories, divisions and districts.

item.title: South Punjab vs Saraiki Province vs Bahawalpur: What’s the Difference?
item.description: South Punjab, Saraiki province and Bahawalpur restoration are related but distinct demands. Compare their political goals, regional identities, historical roots and current status.

item.title: Bahawalpur Province Restoration 2026: Why the Demand Is Back
item.description: Why is Bahawalpur demanding restoration as a separate province? Follow the historical argument, the 2026 campaign, the South Punjab distinction and constitutional hurdles.

item.title: Is Gilgit-Baltistan a Province of Pakistan? GB, AJK and Islamabad Explained
item.description: Gilgit-Baltistan is not one of Pakistan’s four constitutional provinces. Learn how GB, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Islamabad Capital Territory and the four provinces differ in legal and administrative status.

item.title: Income Went Up. So Why Does Life Feel Harder? Pakistan's Household Squeeze in the Data
item.description: Empirical research report examining household income, consumption, food insecurity, poverty and purchasing power in Pakistan using HIES 2024–25 data.

item.title: The Price of a Simple Task: How Much Does Pakistan's Bureaucracy Cost Citizens?
item.description: Research report analyzing administrative burden, citizen grievance signals from the Pakistan Citizen's Portal, Mohtasib reports, and introducing the PPRI Administrative Burden Index.

item.title: Same Country, Different Life: How Much Does Your District Determine Your Access to Basic Services?
item.description: Research report investigating geographic inequality across Pakistan's districts in education, clean water access, internet penetration, and household food insecurity.

item.title: The Bribe You Can't See: How Corruption Becomes a Private Tax on Citizens
item.description: Research report conceptualizing corruption as a regressive private tax on public service access, drawing on Transparency International Pakistan survey data and administrative complaint evidence.

item.title: Does Money Work Better When It Is Spent Closer to the People?
item.description: Research report evaluating fiscal decentralization, local government spending benchmarks from the World Bank and OECD, and lessons from intermediate city programmes in Punjab.

item.title: The Provincial Reorganization of Pakistan: Constitutional, Demographic, Fiscal, and Administrative Architecture
item.description: Comprehensive institutional treatise connecting constitutional law, demographic scale, fiscal federalism, administrative transition, and Article 140A devolution in Pakistan.

item.title: Administrative Scale & Civil Service Ratios: Evaluating Field Governance Disparities
item.description: Policy brief examining administrative workload imbalances, officer-to-citizen ratios, and service delivery bottlenecks across Pakistan's 4 provinces.

item.title: Provinces and Local Government: Evaluating Devolution Architectures
item.description: Working paper analyzing the constitutional mandate of Article 140A, statutory Provincial Finance Commission (PFC) awards, and municipal financial empowerment.

item.title: Pakistan Subnational Baseline 2023 & Census Open Datasets
item.description: Authoritative empirical dataset documenting Pakistan's 2017 and 2023 census population benchmarks, land areas, district counts, divisional structures, and NFC transfer parameters.

item.title: Constitution of Pakistan: Statutory Provincial Reader
item.description: Interactive legal reader of the Constitution of Pakistan: examining Articles 1, 140A, 160, and 239 governing provincial reorganization and municipal powers.

item.title: Why Is Pakistan Debating New Provinces Again?
item.description: An empirical examination of the 2026 provincial restructuring debate: population scale, administrative distance, Article 239 supermajorities, and local devolution.

item.title: Four Provinces, 241.5 Million People: Has Pakistan Outgrown Its Administrative Structure?
item.description: Investigating demographic concentration: Punjab's 127.7M population compared to global federations, divisional giants, and governance limits.

item.title: What Would a New Province Actually Change in Pakistan?
item.description: An institutional analysis of provincial machinery: elected assemblies, high court principal seats, civil secretariats, asset division, and transition governance.

item.title: The 18th Amendment: Did Devolution Stop at the Provincial Capital?
item.description: Evaluating whether constitutional decentralisation reached citizens, or resulted in provincial fiscal hoarding and the collapse of municipal local spending.

item.title: Where Does Pakistan's Development Money Go? Federal, Provincial and Local Spending Explained
item.description: Following the public rupee from the federal divisible pool to provincial consolidated funds, recurrent burdens, and municipal service delivery outcomes.

item.title: More Provinces or Stronger Local Governments? Pakistan's Devolution Debate
item.description: Benchmarking territorial reorganization against municipal empowerment across citizen proximity, transition costs, fiscal viability, and daily service delivery.

item.title: South Punjab: Why Does the Province Demand Keep Returning?
item.description: Examining 40.4M citizens, acute UNDP human development disparities, legislative milestones (1970–2026), and the 2020 Secretariat experiment.

item.title: Hazara Province: Why Has the Demand Survived for So Long?
item.description: Analyzing 16 years of post-18th Amendment mobilization, 5.7M population, Article 239 supermajority barriers, and hydropower fiscal viability.

item.title: Karachi and Urban Sindh: Representation, Revenue and Administrative Control
item.description: Dissecting the 20.38M megacity governance mosaic (18+ overlapping agencies), tax attribution debates, and the September 2026 Sindh Assembly resolution.

item.title: How Should Pakistan Evaluate a Proposal for a New Province?
item.description: The PPRI 12-point empirical evaluation rubric: testing proposals across constitutional law, fiscal modeling, administrative capacity, and verifiable outcomes.

item.title: When Development Follows the Capital, People Follow: Urban Congestion Cycle
item.description: Analyzing capital-city pull, public spending disparities (Quetta Rs57k vs Rs12k; Lahore Rs31k vs Rs7k), migration feedback loops, and secondary city polycentric counter-models.

item.title: One Province, Many Needs: How Should a Government Decide Development Budget Priority?
item.description: Dissecting subnational capital allocations across 164 districts: competing allocation principles, political discretion, and interactive formula equalization simulator.

item.title: Why Is Local Government Always the Last Tier to Get Power in Pakistan?
item.description: An examination of Article 140A, municipal finance decline (<5% of public spend), legislative resistance, and the structural political economy behind the fragile third tier.

item.title: Pakistan Has Tried Local Government Again and Again: Why Does the System Keep Disappearing?
item.description: A 70-year comparative analysis of local governance cycles, from Basic Democracies to the 2001 Devolution Plan, civil-military dynamics, and post-18th Amendment statutory churn.

item.title: Did Pakistan’s 2001 Devolution Plan Actually Improve Services? The Evidence Is More Complicated Than You Think
item.description: Rigorous sectoral evaluation across education panels (34 Punjab districts) and national healthcare household surveys (57,000+ homes), isolating key implementation bottlenecks.

item.title: Before Local Government Faded, What Did Pakistanis Think About It?
item.description: Quantitative analysis of the 2004/05 National Social Audit: 46.8% citizen point-of-contact for union councils, 33% female councillor quota impact, and dispute conciliation.

item.title: Where Did the Development Money Go When Pakistan Tried District Government?
item.description: Empirical fiscal analysis of 2001 district budgets: 67/33 PFC formulas, Citizen Community Board 80% matching grants, and the post-2008 provincial budgetary clawback.

item.title: A New Province Can Move the Capital—But Can It Move the Power?
item.description: Analyzing the capital centralization paradox in new province scenarios: avoiding administrative primacy, dispersing public institutions, and empowering local districts.

item.title: Can Pakistan Grow Beyond Its Provincial Capitals? The Case for Stronger Secondary Cities
item.description: A spatial economic blueprint for polycentric urban development: World Bank PICIIP intermediate city results (4.5M residents), municipal tax autonomy, and regional clusters.

item.title: How Far Is Government? The Hidden Cost of Administrative Distance in Pakistan
item.description: Introducing the PPRI Administrative Access Index (AAI): 6 dimensions of distance, travel time isochrones (14h+ in peripheral districts), and service desert mapping.
